synopsis: Claims-Arguments-Evidence (CAE) is identified in both Chapter 12 and the glossary as the main alternative to Goal Structuring Notation (GSN) [f9706, f12252]. Chapter 12 associates CAE with Bloomfield and Netkachova (2014), while the glossary explains that it uses the same three ideas as GSN but different shapes [f9706, f12252]. The booklet recommends either a GSN or CAE sketch of the top-level claim in the plan’s safety-scope section, with a preliminary argument included as an appendix; it does not mandate CAE over GSN [f12255].

relations.note: Both identify CAE as the main alternative to GSN.
Specifies where CAE can be used in the plan and appendix.
